issues.description: Example code calls `node.preview()` but never shows the method exists or what it returns when `preview_fn` is None.
issues.detail: The 'Basic usage' block invokes `training_node.preview()` and `preview.to_dict()` as if they are documented API. If a reader copies this and `preview_fn` was never set, what happens? Doc shows the happy path only. Either link to the API reference for `Node.preview()` or state the contract: return type, None behavior, exceptions. Otherwise readers will file bugs.

issues.description: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is gratuitously clever where `pipeline.nodes[0]` would do.
issues.detail: This is documentation. The first example a user reads sets the house style. Using a generator expression with `next()` to grab the first element of a list teaches bad taste. Write `pipeline.nodes[0]` or name the node and look it up. Don't make the reader parse Python idioms unrelated to what's being documented.

issues.description: ImagePreview example has unreachable code after `return` with no warning to the reader.
issues.detail: The function returns the URL form, then has commented-out 'Or a data URI' code below the return. A reader skimming sees two options visually but only one is reachable. Either split into two separate functions or restructure as an if/else. As written, this is the kind of copy-paste hazard that produces broken examples in user code.

issues.description: Best practice says 'Handle errors: wrap preview logic in try-except if needed' without saying what to return on failure.
issues.detail: Vague advice is worse than no advice. If `preview_fn` raises, what does `node.preview()` do? Does Kedro-Viz get a partial render, an empty preview, or a stack trace? The doc should state the framework's behavior on preview failure so users know whether their try-except is required or theatre.

issues.description: PR checklist admits no tests added and no RELEASE.md entry; this is docs-only but the unchecked boxes should be acknowledged.
issues.detail: The PR body has unchecked 'Added tests' and 'RELEASE.md' boxes. For a docs-only change tests may not apply, but a release note for new user-facing documentation usually does. Either tick the boxes with justification or add the RELEASE.md line. Don't leave the checklist half-done; it signals the author didn't finish.

issues.description: Adding lowercase `polars` to the spellcheck ignore list when `Polars` is already there papers over a real Vale rule mismatch.
issues.detail: `Polars` was already accepted. Adding `polars` because the doc happens to use lowercase in a variable name suggests the Vale rule should be case-insensitive or the doc should use the branded capitalization in prose. Fix the rule or the prose, don't grow the ignore list one casing at a time.

review.summary: Docs-only patch adding a section on `preview_fn` to nodes.md plus two trivial Vale config tweaks. The diff is scoped, readable, and matches the existing docs voice — this is what a single-purpose patch looks like. The taste problems are in the example code: clever idioms where direct ones would teach better, unreachable code after a return, and an undocumented `node.preview()` contract that users will hit edge cases on. NEEDS-WORK: fix the example code, tighten the framework-behavior gaps, finish the PR checklist or justify the gaps. The Vale ignore-list addition is a smell but not load-bearing.
